A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 19-page versions of MemOCR. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA evaluations, training and layout ablations, runtime measurements, statistical analyses, and failure cases.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The rich-text drafting and visual reading pipeline, Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, three training tasks, and weighted GRPO optimization remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both train on HotpotQA and evaluate HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Natural Questions, and TriviaQA. The represented tasks and long-context scenarios are unchanged; newly cited benchmarks are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Qwen2.5, R1-DistillQwen, Qwen2.5-1M, Mem0, Mem-α, and MemAgent. The layout, oracle, runtime, and larger-backbone comparisons also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 revises the stated training platform from 64 NVIDIA A100 GPUs to 64 H800 GPUs. The reported 14 days, approximately 1,000 steps, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. This is a reported setting revision, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The layout-removal tests, oracle evidence injections, evidence-density analysis, training-objective ablations, larger-backbone analysis, and successful and failed case studies are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both report three independent evaluation runs, means and standard deviations in Table 6, and independent two-sample t-tests in Table 7. The renderer benchmark also retains five runs of 50 samples each.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings in Tables 1–2 and 6–10 and Figures 4–8 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains 74.6% for MemOCR versus 67.8% for MemAgent at 10K context and a 1024-token budget.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, memory-budget constraints, optimization equations, and Appendix D.2 complexity assumptions and derivations remain unchanged, including Equations 1–13.

C1.justification: Both retain the central claims of adaptive information density through visual layout, robustness under tight budgets, and approximately eightfold effective context utilization. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion do not substantively redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations, failure explanations, and Appendix B limitations remain unchanged. The new conclusion sentence directs readers to those existing limitations without adding a substantive qualification.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the advertised code location from syr-cn/MemOCR to meituan/MemOCR. Appendix C.2 changes the reported GPU model from A100 to H800; other implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds citations to DeepResearch Bench, Gated Recurrent Memory, VTC-R1, and VTCBench, and explicitly names the already-cited AgentOCR. These additions modestly extend related-work coverage without substantially revising the research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 adds a limitations cross-reference in Section 5, makes limited wording and citation edits in Appendix A, updates the preprint date, and changes 'Fig. 5' to 'Figure 5'. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds LongCat branding to the title page and running headers and adjusts spacing and pagination around figures, tables, and text. The eight research figures and ten tables retain their scientific content; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Acknowledging additional memory and visual-compression research, particularly VTC-R1 and VTCBench in Appendix A, modestly improves the paper's research context. The conclusion also makes existing limitations easier to find. These benefits are limited: the method, empirical results, and statistical support remain unchanged.
